1. [Maximum mark: 16]
(a) Draw the Cayley table for the set of integers $G=\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ under addition modulo 6, $+_6$. [3 marks]
(b) Show that $\{G, +_6\}$ is a group. [4 marks]
(c) Find the order of each element. [3 marks]
(d) Show that $\{G, +_6\}$ is cyclic and state its generators. [2 marks]
(e) Find a subgroup with three elements. [2 marks]
(f) Find the other proper subgroups of $\{G, +_6\}$. [2 marks]

2.text_clean:
2. [Maximum mark: 13]
(a) Below are the graphs of the two functions $f: P \to Q$ and $g: A \to B$.
[Graph f: cubic-shaped curve; domain P is a bold interval on the x-axis, codomain Q a bold interval on the y-axis; the curve rises, levels off below the x-axis, then rises steeply. Graph g: increasing concave curve over a bold interval A on the x-axis; codomain B a bold interval on the y-axis extending below the x-axis, while the curve stays above it.]
Determine, with reference to features of the graphs, whether the functions are injective and/or surjective. [4 marks]
(b) Given two functions $h: X \to Y$ and $k: Y \to Z$.
Show that
(i) if both $h$ and $k$ are injective then so is the composite function $k \circ h$;
(ii) if both $h$ and $k$ are surjective then so is the composite function $k \circ h$. [9 marks]

3.text_clean:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]
Prove that $(A \cap B) \setminus (A \cap C) = A \cap (B \setminus C)$ where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are three subsets of the universal set $U$.

4.text_clean:
4. [Maximum mark: 19]
(a) The relation $aRb$ is defined on $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}$ if and only if $ab$ is the square of a positive integer.
(i) Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation.
(ii) Find the equivalence classes of $R$ that contain more than one element. [10 marks]
(b) Given the group $(G, *)$, a subgroup $(H, *)$ and $a, b \in G$, we define $a \sim b$ if and only if $ab^{-1} \in H$. Show that $\sim$ is an equivalence relation. [9 marks]

5. [Maximum mark: 6]
(a) Write down why the table below is a Latin square. [2 marks]
| | d | e | b | a | c |
| d | c | d | e | b | a |
| e | d | e | b | a | c |
| b | a | b | d | c | e |
| a | b | a | c | e | d |
| c | e | c | a | d | b |
(b) Use Lagrange's theorem to show that the table is not a group table. [4 marks]
